transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because people keep getting on my case about not listening. 

My wife, or my supervisor at the plant... they'll be talking straight to me, and... I don't know. A minute later I realize I only caught half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to say it all over again. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
How long has this problem with not listening or paying attention been going on?

Um... I guess about two years. Two years and a couple of months, maybe. 

It's just been this bad since... well, since my wife started working outside the home. I had to start handling more of the schedule on my own, and... yeah. Since then.
Besides the listening problem, how has your mood been over these past two years? Have you been feeling down, sad, or depressed?
Uh... no. Not really. My mood's been fine, I guess. I'm not... depressed or anything. Just normal.
Besides work and conversations with your wife, do you notice this attention problem in other situations — like when you're watching TV, reading, or doing hobbies you enjoy?
Uh... no, not really. I don't... I don't read much anyway. But if I'm just watching TV or doing my own thing, it's fine. I haven't really noticed it then. Just... mostly what I said before.

When you're doing something you really enjoy or find interesting — like a hobby, a sport, or something you're passionate about — do you have trouble staying focused on that, or does your attention seem fine?
No... it's fine. Like I just said, if it's something I actually want to do, I don't really have a problem with it. It's just... fine.

When your wife or supervisor are talking to you about things you need to pay attention to — like instructions or important information — do you find yourself thinking about other things, or does your mind just kind of... drift off?
Uh... no, not really. I don't... I don't just sit there daydreaming or anything. I hear them talking. It's not like my mind goes somewhere else.

When your wife or supervisor are talking to you, do you feel like you're making an effort to listen and focus, but it's hard to keep up — or does it feel more like you're just not interested in what they're saying?
I mean... I hear them. I'm trying to listen. It's just... I don't know. I guess it's just hard to keep up sometimes. It's not that I don't care. I just... I don't know.
Before your wife started working outside the home — say, three years ago or more — did you ever have problems like this with listening or paying attention to people at work or at home?

Yeah, I guess. It's... it's always been like this. Even when I was a kid. Teachers were always moving my desk because I couldn't just sit there. I'd blurt things out, or... I don't know, get in trouble for messing with other kids' stuff. That was all way before middle school. So... yeah. Always been this way.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports lifelong inattention symptoms (since childhood with teacher complaints about seat movement, blurting out, and fidgeting) that have persisted into adulthood. Current presentation includes difficulty sustaining attention during conversations with wife and supervisor, though symptoms are selective (not present during preferred activities). The chronic, pervasive nature since childhood, combined with current functional impairment in work and marital contexts, supports Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive type.
